title: A word on this preface and its readers
source_text: Τοῦτο δὲ τὸ προοίμιον μετὰ τὸ ὑπαγορεῦσαι πάντα τὰ μέχρι τῆς παρὰ Κέλσῳ τοῦ Ἰουδαίου πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν προσωποποιΐας ἔδοξεν ἡμῖν προτάξαι τῆς ἀρχῆς· ἵν᾿ αὐτῷ προεντυγχάνῃ ὁ ἀναγνωσόμενος τὰ πρὸς Κέλσον ἡμῖν ὑπαγορευθέντα καὶ ἴδῃ ὅτι οὐ πάνυ πιστοῖς γέγραπται τὸ βιβλίον τοῦτο ἀλλ᾿ ἢ τέλεον ἀγεύστοις τῆς εἰς Χριστὸν πίστεως ἢ τοῖς, ὡς ὁ ἀπόστολος ὠνόμασεν, ἀσθενοῦσιν ἐν „τῇ πίστει.“ εἶπε δ᾿ οὕτως· „τὸν δ᾿ ἀσθενοῦντα τῇ πίστει προσλαμβάνεσθε.“ ἀπολογησάσθω δὲ τὸ προοίμιον, ὅτι ἄλλῃ μὲν προθέσει τὴν ἀρχὴν τῶν πρὸς Κέλσον ὑπηγορεύσαμεν ἄλλῃ δὲ τὰ μετὰ τὴν ἀρχήν. πρότερον μὲν γὰρ ἐσκοποῦμεν ὑποσημειώσασθαι τὰ κεφάλαια καὶ διὰ βραχέων τὰ πρὸς αὐτὰ λεγόμενα, εἶτα μετὰ τοῦτο σωματοποιῆσαι τὸν λόγον· ὕστερον δ᾿ αὐτὰ τὰ πράγματα ὑπέβαλεν ἡμῖν φειδομένοις χρόνου ἀρκεσθῆναι μὲν τοῖς κατὰ τὴν ἀρχὴν οὕτως ὑπαγορευθεῖσιν, ἐν δὲ τοῖς ἑξῆς κατὰ τὸ δυνατὸν ἡμῖν συγγραφικῶς ἀγωνίσασθαι πρὸς τὰ Κέλσου καθ᾿ ἡμῶν ἐγκλήματα. διόπερ αἰτοῦμεν συγγνώμην ἐπὶ τῇ ἀρχῇ τῶν μετὰ τὸ προοίμιον. ἐὰν δὲ μὴ κινηθῇς καὶ ὑπὸ τῶν ἑξῆς ὑπαγορευθέντων ἀνυσίμως, καὶ ἐπ᾿ αὐτοῖς τὴν ὁμοίαν συγγνώμην αἰτῶν ἀναπέμπω σε, ἐάνπερ ἔτι θέλῃς δι᾿ ὑπαγορεύσεων τὰς λύσεις σοι τῶν Κέλσου γενέσθαι λόγων, ἐπὶ τοὺς ἡμῶν συνετωτέρους καὶ δυνατοὺς, διὰ λέξεων καὶ βιβλίων ἀνατρέπειν δυναμένους τὰ καθ᾿ ἡμῶν τοῦ Κέλσου ἐγκλήματα. πλὴν βελτίων ὁ μηδὲ τὴν ἀρχὴν δεηθεὶς, κἂν ἐντυχὼν τῷ Κέλσου συγγράμματι, τῆς πρὸς αὐτὸ ἀπολογίας, ἀλλ᾿ ὑπερφρονήσας πάντα τὰ ἐν τῷ βιβλίῳ αὐτοῦ ὡς καὶ ὑπὸ τοῦ τυχόντος ἐν Χριστῷ πιστοῦ διὰ τὸ ἐν αὐτῷ πνεῦμα εὐλόγως καταφρονούμενα.
pass_a_gloss: This preface (προοίμιον), after dictating (ὑπαγορεύω) all things up to the impersonation (προσωποποιΐα) in Celsus of the Jew [speaking] toward Jesus, seemed good to us to place before (προτάσσω) the beginning (ἀρχή); so that the one who will read (ἀναγιγνώσκω) the things dictated by us toward Celsus may meet (ἐντυγχάνω) it first, and see that this book is written not at all (οὐ πάνυ) for believers (πιστοί) but either for those wholly untasted (ἄγευστος) of faith in Christ or for those whom, as the apostle named them, are weak (ἀσθενέω) in 'the faith'. He said thus: [Rom 14:1: receive/welcome (προσλαμβάνω) the one weak in the faith]. Let the preface make defence/excuse (ἀπολογέομαι) that with one purpose (πρόθεσις) we dictated the beginning of [the reply] to Celsus, and with another the things after the beginning. For first we aimed (σκοπέω) to note down (ὑποσημειόω) the headings (κεφάλαια) and briefly the things said against them, then after this to give body to (σωματοποιέω) the discourse (λόγος); but later the matters themselves suggested (ὑποβάλλω) to us, sparing (φείδομαι) time, to be content (ἀρκέομαι) with the things thus dictated at the beginning, but in what follows, as far as possible for us, to contend (ἀγωνίζομαι) in treatise form (συγγραφικῶς) against Celsus's charges against us. Wherefore we ask pardon (συγγνώμη) for the beginning of what follows the preface. And if you are not moved (κινέω) effectually (ἀνυσίμως) even by the things dictated next, asking the like pardon for them too, I send you on (ἀναπέμπω), if indeed you still wish the solutions (λύσεις) of Celsus's arguments to come to you through dictations, to those wiser (συνετώτεροι) than us and able (δυνατοί), able to overturn (ἀνατρέπω) through words/speech (λέξεις) and books Celsus's charges against us. But better is the one who did not at all (τὴν ἀρχήν) need, even having read (ἐντυγχάνω) Celsus's treatise, the defence against it, but having looked down on (ὑπερφρονέω) all things in his book as reasonably (εὐλόγως) despised (καταφρονέω) even by the ordinary (ὁ τυχών) believer in Christ because of the Spirit (πνεῦμα) in him.
pass_b_english: We decided to place this preface before the beginning after we had dictated everything up to the point where Celsus introduces his Jew addressing Jesus. We did so in order that whoever is going to read our dictated reply to Celsus may come upon it first, and may see that this book has not been written for believers at all, but either for those who have had no taste of faith in Christ, or for those whom the apostle called weak “in the faith.” His words are these: “Welcome the one who is weak in the faith” (Romans 14:1).

And let the preface make this excuse: that we dictated the beginning of our reply to Celsus with one plan, and what follows the beginning with another. At first we meant to note down the main points and, briefly, our replies to them, and after that to give the argument its full body. But later the work itself suggested to us, as we wished to save time, that we should be content with what had been dictated in this way at the beginning, and in what followed should contend against the charges Celsus brings against us, as far as we could, in the manner of a written treatise. That is why we ask pardon for the beginning of what follows the preface.

And if even what we dictated next does not move you to good effect, then I ask the same pardon for that too, and I send you on, if you still wish to have answers to Celsus’s arguments in dictated form, to those who are wiser than we are, and able to overturn Celsus’s charges against us in words and in books. Better, however, is the one who, even if he has read Celsus’s treatise, has had no need at all of a defence against it, but has looked down on everything in his book as things that even an ordinary believer in Christ rightly despises, because of the Spirit within him.

choices.choice: 'μέχρι τῆς παρὰ Κέλσῳ τοῦ Ἰουδαίου πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν προσωποποιΐας' refers to the point where Celsus introduces his imaginary Jew addressing Jesus (Book 1.28); rendered 'up to the point where Celsus brings on his Jew to speak to Jesus'. 'οὐ πάνυ πιστοῖς' rendered 'not ... for believers at all'; a weaker reading ('not for those who are fully believers') is possible, since the weak in faith are named as readers, but 'not at all' is the usual force of οὐ πάνυ in this period. 'ἀγεύστοις τῆς εἰς Χριστὸν πίστεως' rendered 'who have had no taste of faith in Christ'. 'ὑπαγορεύω / ὑπαγόρευσις' = dictate / dictation (Origen dictated to scribes); kept. 'συγγραφικῶς' = in the manner of a written treatise, as against brief notes; rendered 'in the form of a full treatise'. 'διὰ λέξεων καὶ βιβλίων' rendered 'by speech and by books'. 'τὸ ἐν αὐτῷ πνεῦμα' taken as the Holy Spirit dwelling in the believer, hence 'Spirit' capitalised. No LXX renumbering needed.

anf_compare.notes: Crombie (ANF 1872) and Chadwick (1953) were not used or consulted; the English is from the Greek.

reviewer: claude (independent clause-by-clause pass against the Greek)

changes: 'brings on his Jew to speak to Jesus' -> 'introduces his Jew addressing Jesus' (προσωποποιΐα; attribution 'his Jew' kept)
'Let the preface also make this excuse' -> 'And let the preface make this excuse' ('also' was added)
'what could be said in answer to them' -> 'our replies to them' (τὰ πρὸς αὐτὰ λεγόμενα; 'could' was added modality); 'and then, after that' -> 'and after that'
'as we were sparing of time' -> 'as we wished to save time'; 'in the form of a full treatise' -> 'in the manner of a written treatise' (συγγραφικῶς; 'full' was added)

'you are not effectually moved' -> 'what we dictated next does not move you to good effect' (ἀνυσίμως); 'refer you' -> 'send you on' (ἀναπέμπω); 'receive by dictation the solutions' -> 'have answers ... in dictated form' (λύσεις)
'by speech and by books' -> 'in words and in books' (διὰ λέξεων καὶ βιβλίων)

'has no need ... looks down' -> 'has had no need ... has looked down' (aorists δεηθείς, ὑπερφρονήσας); 'even the most ordinary believer' -> 'even an ordinary believer' (ὁ τυχών; superlative was added); 'with good reason' -> 'rightly' (εὐλόγως)

Checked Romans 14:1 (τὸν δὲ ἀσθενοῦντα τῇ πίστει προσλαμβάνεσθε): matches. 'οὐ πάνυ πιστοῖς' kept as 'not for believers at all', as the translator argued; the reading 'not for firm believers' is possible and is noted in translator_notes
